text:
Adam Engstrom is a 22-year-old Swedish defenseman in his first real stretch of NHL games, and he's already in trade rumors: TSN's Darren Dreger mentioned him as a possible piece in talks around Detroit's Dylan Larkin, whose refusal to play until traded is the Red Wings' story of the season. Engstrom scored his first NHL goal against Utah on Nov 5.

He's played 13 games, about 11 minutes a night, often going in and out of the lineup as Mike Matheson came and went. Montreal takes 54% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, about 5 points better than without him, and the Canadiens have scored 4.1 more goals than expected during his shifts, so his on-ice results look a little better than the play.

He was a third-round pick in 2022 and had 22 points in 51 SHL games in 2023-24 before moving to North America, which translates to about 23 over 82 NHL games. With Matheson injured again, his spot should be safer for a while. Our talent range has him around 11 points. Our model compares him to Utah's Dmitri Simashev, another young defenseman in limited minutes.
